expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: old pods are still running `SELECT ... legacy_email` against a schema where it no longer exists. Every request through those three paths 500s

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: You're at step 5 of expand/contract... Ship the code-only PR today... drop the column Tuesday

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: `git revert` brings back the code, not the bytes — those are gone the moment the migration runs

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: Your only restore path is a backup... The drop: needs a restore, two people, and hours

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: The skill's line is that timing is about staffing and recovery speed, not superstition

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: a CI check that fails any PR whose migrations contain `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, or `ALTER ... DROP` unless the PR carries an explicit approval label

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "CI is green" proves nothing about the column

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: Steps 1–4 are reversible; step 5 gets its own deploy precisely because it isn't
